newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares jump 2.98pct, extend rebound.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares jump 2.98pct, extend rebound.

text.p: Greek shares continued strong on Wednesday, jumping nearly three percent in a broadly-based recovery which started in the previous session.
Fund managers said the sharp 300-pont correction in the benchmark index during the course of one month was larger than expected.

"The correction was expected, and indeed desirable to let the market breathe after this year's rally, but turned out deeper than expected," said Alexandros Sarrigeorgiou, fund manager at Allianz Mutual Funds.
"Had the market climbed further in late May, the correction would have been more traumatic to sentiment," he added. "It is important that the technical 1,450-point support level held strong."
Market participants longed for the next wave of corporate results.

"The next market-moving event will come in the form of corporate announcements on interim results, validating expectations for improved 1997 profits and affering a yardstick for 1998 results," said Sarrigeorgiou.
Sentiment was not hurt by proposals of government officials for a higher contribution of Greece's corporate sector to the broader economic recovery effort.
Industry Minister Vasso Papandreou said on Tuesday she favoured a tax on corporate earnings to raise funds for jobs training to fight unemployment.
This came after an economic policy report submitted last week by professor Yiannis Spraos, economic advisor to prime minister Costas Simitis.
The report called for tough fiscal and incomes policy measures including a one-off 10 percent tax on corporate profits in 1998.
But National Economy Minister Yiannos Papandoniou made clear the government was not considering adopting such a measure.
"Some investors may trade onf such vague proposals, but a more appropriate strategy is to take a longer term view on policy and corporate prospects," said Sarrigeorgiou.

On Wendesday, Salomon Brothers said in its June global equity strategy report that Greek equities were overbought and expected to remain at current levels in the short-term following this year's rally.
Salomon also anticipated Athens to continue outperforming emerging market indices on continuing positive results from sound macroeconomic policies.
It said industrial stocks would outperforming banks reversing current price differential trends.
The Athens general index climbed 2.88 percent or 43.17 points from Tuesday's 1,498.94 to settle at 1,542.11, near the day's high.
All sub-indices showed gains, with construction leading with a 4.09 percent appreciation.
Banks and industrials were also strong, up 3.88 and 3.14 percent, respectively.
Turnover rose to 22.1 billion drachmas on volume of 6.8 million shares.
Trading included a 1.1 million share block of small-cap hatchery Riopesca which changed hands at 2,000 drachmas.
Advancers led decliners 182 to 43 with 19 shares unchanged on 244 traded.

The ING Baring Financial Products American style call warrant based on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $75.14-$76.84. The strike price is set at $99.60 and the warrants expire October 8, 1997.

The ING Baring Financial Products American-style call warrant on a basket of six blue-chips denominated in drachmas was quoted at 3,124-3,338 drachmas. The strike price is set at 10,000 drachmas and the warrants expire on February 2, 1998.
The ING Baring American-style second call warrant on a basket of six bank stocks was quoted at $13.30-N/O. The strike price is set at $110.0 and the warrants expire April 9 1998.

The recently launched ING Baring American-style, drachma- denominated call warrant on the bourse's benchmark index was quoted at 215-246 drachmas. The strike price is set at 1,639 points and the warrants expire May 14 1998.
